Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Acute shortness of breath with wheeze and cough for 2–3 days; dyspnea with brisk walking; able to talk but limited by breathlessness.
- History of present illness: Wheezing and coughing started 2–3 days ago during a run; blue (short-acting) inhaler used with little relief; currently using inhalers (as needed and for prevention). Reports using blue inhaler daily and/or to prevent symptoms (morning/evening).
- Past medical history: Asthma; eczema; hay fever (allergic rhinitis). Family history: brother with asthma; sister with eczema. Last asthma review ~2 years ago; last asthma attack ~3–4 years ago.
- Medications (current): Inhaled corticosteroid (brown inhaler) – Clenil (beclomethasone) – currently used; Salbutamol (blue reliever) – used as needed and as prevention; Topical preparations (cetraz? cetraben emollient and hydrocortisone) as per prior regimen; dosing not documented for these.
- Allergies: Hay fever noted as an allergic condition; no known drug allergies reported.
- Social history: Not specified.
- Additional notes: Peak flow at baseline previously reported as approximately 380 (no current peak flow provided at visit).

Objective:
- Physical examination: Not yet performed at this visit; planned to examine chest and perform peak flow during the encounter.
- Investigations/measurements planned: Chest examination; peak flow measurement during the visit.
- Current objective data: Baseline peak flow previously reported as ~380; no current vitals or exam findings documented.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Asthma, acute exacerbation / poorly controlled asthma
   - Assessment: Likely asthma exacerbation given new/worsening dyspnea, wheeze, and current reliance on reliever inhaler with limited effect.
   - Differential diagnoses (if applicable): Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction; allergic bronchitis/viral bronchitis (less likely given history but considered).
   - Investigations planned: Chest examination; peak flow measurement during this visit; monitoring of response to therapy.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Increase inhaled corticosteroid (brown inhaler, Clenil) to 4 puffs twice daily.
     - Continue salbutamol (blue reliever) as needed; instruction to use up to every 2 hours if symptoms persist, with the warning that frequent use indicates poor control.
     - Advise if breathing worsens or not improving to go to A&E (emergency department) immediately.
     - Interim follow-up: GP appointment to review asthma within the next few days.
   - Relevant referrals: Schedule a GP (or asthma nurse) follow-up within a few days for asthma review.

Quality checks (document quality and transcript clarity):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (BP, HR, RR, O2 saturation) and objective respiratory Exam findings not documented.
  - Current peak flow measurement during this visit (only baseline prior value mentioned).
  - Comprehensive medication reconciliation (doses/routes/frequencies for all medications not consistently documented; some names repeated/confused in transcript).
  - Smoking status and immunization status not documented.
- Internal conflicts noted:
  - Transcript shows conflicting statements: one line indicates “fever,” which is later clarified as “hay fever.” Mark as conflict noted.
  - Medication names/brands appear inconsistently (e.g., “Flanel Bactroban,” then “Cetraben” with hydrocortisone); clinician should verify current medications.
- Transcript quality:
  - Conversation includes some typos/ambiguities and incomplete medication details; clinical plan relies on stated intents (e.g., increase Clenil to 4 puffs bid) and requires confirmatory dosing during follow-up.
